zh: 次釋超越三昧。今明超越三昧者，如《般若經》中說：「行者因師子奮迅三昧，逆順出入超越三昧。云何超越三昧？離諸欲惡、不善法，有覺有觀，離生喜樂，入初禪；從初禪起，超入非有想；非有想起，入非無想處；非無想處起，入滅受想定；滅受想定起，還入初禪；從初禪起，入滅受想定；滅受想定起，入二禪；二禪起，入滅受想定；滅受想定起，入三禪；三禪起，入滅受想定；滅受想定起，入四禪；四禪起，入滅受想定；滅受想定起，入虛空處；虛空處起，入滅受想定；滅受想定起，入識處；識處起，入滅受想定；滅受想定起，入無所有處；無所有處起，入滅受想定；滅受想定起，入非有想；非有想起，入非無想處；非無想處起，入滅受想定。
en: Next, explaining the samādhi of transcendence. Here, clarifying the samādhi of transcendence: as explained in the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra: "The practitioner, through the lion's-frolic samādhi, enters and leaves the samādhi of transcendence, both forward and backward. What is meant by the samādhi of transcendence?

Departing from every desire, evil, and unwholesome dharma, possessing initial thought and sustained reflection, with joy and happiness born of separation, entering the first dhyāna; rising from the first dhyāna, transcending directly into neither-perception; rising from neither-perception, entering non-not-perception; rising from non-not-perception, entering the concentration of the cessation of sensation and perception; rising from the concentration of the cessation of sensation and perception, entering back into the first dhyāna; rising from the first dhyāna, entering the concentration of the cessation of sensation and perception; rising from that concentration, entering the second dhyāna; rising from the second dhyāna, entering that concentration; rising from that concentration, entering the third dhyāna; rising from the third dhyāna, entering that concentration; rising from that concentration, entering the fourth dhyāna; rising from the fourth dhyāna, entering that concentration; rising from that concentration, entering the sphere of space; rising from the sphere of space, entering that concentration; rising from that concentration, entering the sphere of consciousness; rising from the sphere of consciousness, entering that concentration; rising from that concentration, entering the sphere of nothingness; rising from the sphere of nothingness, entering that concentration; rising from that concentration, entering neither-perception; rising from neither-perception, entering non-not-perception; rising from non-not-perception, entering that concentration once more.

zh: 從滅受想定起，入散心中；散心中起，入滅受想定；滅受想定起，還入散心中；散心中起，入非有想；非有想起，入非無想處；非無想處起，住散心中；散心中起，入第四禪中；第四禪中起，住散心中；散心中起，入第三禪中；第三禪中起，住散心中；散心中起，入第二禪；第二禪起，住散心中；散心中起，入初禪；初禪起，住散心中。是超越三昧。」今明超越之相，自有超入、超出相，如前二番經文說。超入、出中，各有四種：一者、順入超；二者、逆入超；三者、順逆入超；四者、逆順入超。超出亦如是。
en: Rising from the concentration of the cessation of sensation and perception, entering the scattered mind; rising from the scattered mind, entering that concentration; rising from that concentration, entering back into the scattered mind; rising from the scattered mind, entering neither-perception; rising from neither-perception, entering non-not-perception; rising from non-not-perception, abiding in the scattered mind; rising from the scattered mind, entering the fourth dhyāna; rising from the fourth dhyāna, abiding in the scattered mind; rising from the scattered mind, entering the third dhyāna; rising from the third dhyāna, abiding in the scattered mind; rising from the scattered mind, entering the second dhyāna; rising from the second dhyāna, abiding in the scattered mind; rising from the scattered mind, entering the first dhyāna; rising from the first dhyāna, abiding in the scattered mind. This is the samādhi of transcendence."

Here, clarifying the mark of transcendence itself: there is, of itself, the mark of transcending inward and the mark of transcending outward, as explained in the two passages of scripture given above. Within transcending inward and transcending outward, each, alike, has four kinds: first, forward transcendence, entering; second, backward transcendence, entering; third, forward-then-backward transcendence, entering; fourth, backward-then-forward transcendence, entering. Transcending outward follows this same pattern as well.

zh: 復次，此超越三昧中，復有傍超。傍超亦有四種，類如前說。譬如師子有四種趠：一者、前擲四十里，即譬順超之相；二者、却擲四十里，即譬逆超之相；三者、右傍擲四十里，即譬傍超入根本禪定之相；四者、左傍擲四十里，即譬傍超入觀禪之相。復有二種超越：一者、具足超；二者、不具足超。具足超，即是菩薩超越，如上所說。不具足超，即是聲聞超越三昧，不能自在，遠超入故。故《摩訶衍》云：「譬如黃師子、白師子，二俱能趠。若黃師子趠，則不遠；若白師子，則能遠擲。聲聞之人入超越三昧，但能從初禪超入三禪，尚不能超二，何能超三？此則如黃師子之超。菩薩不爾，從於初禪逈能超入滅受想定，隨意自在，此則如白師子之超。」
en: Furthermore, within this very samādhi of transcendence, there is, further, sideways transcendence as well. Sideways transcendence, too, has four kinds, following the same pattern as already given above. It is like the lion, which has four kinds of leap: first, leaping forward forty li — this illustrates the mark of forward transcendence; second, leaping backward forty li — this illustrates the mark of backward transcendence; third, leaping sideways to the right forty li — this illustrates the mark of sideways transcendence into the root dhyāna concentrations; fourth, leaping sideways to the left forty li — this illustrates the mark of sideways transcendence into contemplative dhyāna.

There are, further, two kinds of transcendence: first, complete transcendence; second, incomplete transcendence. Complete transcendence is precisely the bodhisattva's own transcendence, as already explained above. Incomplete transcendence is precisely the śrāvaka's own samādhi of transcendence, unable to move freely, since it can transcend across only a short distance. Hence the Mahāyāna treatise says: "It is like the yellow lion and the white lion, both, alike, able to leap. Should the yellow lion leap, it does not go far; should the white lion leap, it is able to leap a great distance. The śrāvaka, entering the samādhi of transcendence, is able only to transcend from the first dhyāna directly into the third — unable even to transcend across two stages, how much less three? This, then, is like the yellow lion's own leap. The bodhisattva is not so: from the first dhyāna, he is able to transcend directly all the way into the concentration of the cessation of sensation and perception, moving freely at will — this, then, is like the white lion's own leap."

The samādhi of transcendence takes the lion's-frolic samādhi's back-and-forth motion and adds true discontinuity — leaping directly from the first dhyāna to neither-perception-nor-non-perception, skipping every intermediate stage, and then, in the sequence's second half, alternating in a fixed, stated order between deep concentration and "the scattered mind" (the ordinary waking state) itself, treated here as just one more station in the sequence rather than a lapse from it. The yellow-lion/white-lion simile closing the section is the treatise's sharpest image yet for the difference between śrāvaka and bodhisattva attainment of the identical samādhi: not a different practice, but a different range — the śrāvaka's leap reaches only the third dhyāna, while the bodhisattva's reaches all the way to the cessation of sensation and perception in a single bound.

items.zh: 大力阿羅漢 · 二十五三昧 · 卷第十竟

zh: 若三乘行人入此三昧，具足修一切法門，是時觀定等法，轉深明利，更復出生百千三昧，功德深厚，神通猛利，故名觀禪。亦有鍊禪、自在定。鍊禪，如上說。自在定者，於諸法門自在出、入、住，轉變見八自在也。亦名頂禪，於諸禪中最為高極，則能轉壽為福，轉福為壽，故復名佛智三昧，欲知隨願，即知三世事，二處攝，謂欲界、四禪。復有無諍三昧，令他心不起諍；五處攝：欲界及四禪。復有四辯：法、詞辯，二處攝，謂欲界、初禪；義辯、樂說辯，九地攝，謂欲界、四禪、無色定。復有五神通、十四變化心、十八變化，皆如前說。若禪中欲聞、見、觸時，皆用梵世識，識滅則止。
en: Should a practitioner of the three vehicles enter this samādhi, becoming complete in the cultivation of every dharma-gate, at that time the dharmas of contemplation and concentration alike grow ever deeper, brighter, and sharper, further giving rise to a hundred, a thousand samādhis, their merit deep and abundant, their supernormal power fierce and sharp — hence this is named contemplative dhyāna.

There is, further, the refining dhyāna and mastery over concentration. The refining dhyāna is as already explained above. Mastery over concentration means being free to leave, enter, and abide within every dharma-gate at will, transforming and manifesting the eight kinds of mastery. This is also named the summit dhyāna, being the very highest and utmost among every dhyāna, able to turn lifespan into merit and merit into lifespan — hence it is, further, named the buddha-wisdom samādhi: wishing to know something according to one's own aspiration, one thereby knows matters of the three times at once, included within two stages, namely the desire realm and the fourth dhyāna.

There is, further, the samādhi free of contention, causing another's own mind to give rise to no contention at all, included within five stages: the desire realm and the four dhyānas. There are, further, the four kinds of eloquence: eloquence in dharma and eloquence in expression, included within two stages, namely the desire realm and the first dhyāna; eloquence in meaning and eloquence in ready speech, included within nine stages, namely the desire realm, the four dhyānas, and the four formless concentrations. There are, further, the five supernormal powers, the fourteen transformations of mind, and the eighteen transformations, all as already explained above. Should one, within dhyāna, wish to hear, see, or touch something, one uses, in every case, the consciousness belonging to the Brahmā world; once this consciousness ceases, this, too, ceases.

zh: 復次，是諸禪中皆有三十七品、三解脫門、四諦十六行觀、十一智、三無漏根，如是等智行，在下當分別。若二乘人具此諸禪者，即是俱解脫；事、理具足，成就無累，故亦名不壞解脫；具足成就出世間諸禪定法故，具足三明、六通及八解脫等一切諸大功德，故名大力阿羅漢也。若是菩薩於正觀心中入此三昧，得諸法等相，即得二十五三昧，能破二十五有，住王三昧，一切三昧悉入其中，是時亦名禪波羅蜜滿。此則略說三乘共禪行行法門竟。是中法門無量，令欲更詮入道要行，豈得具說耶？
釋禪波羅蜜次第法門卷第十
en: Furthermore, within all these dhyānas there are, present throughout, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the three liberation-gates, the Four Noble Truths' own sixteen practices of contemplation, the eleven kinds of wisdom, and the three undefiled faculties — wisdom and practice of this kind shall be distinguished further below.

Should a practitioner of the two vehicles become complete with all these dhyānas, this is precisely liberation-in-both-respects: phenomena and principle both complete, its accomplishment free of any entanglement whatsoever — hence this, too, is named the indestructible liberation; complete in the accomplishment of every world-transcending dhyāna concentration dharma, complete with the three insights, the six supernormal powers, and the eight liberations, and every other great merit — hence this is named the great-strength arhat.

Should this be a bodhisattva, entering this samādhi within the correctly contemplating mind, obtaining the equal mark of every dharma, he thereby obtains the twenty-five samādhis, able to break through the twenty-five states of existence, abiding in the king of samādhis, every samādhi entirely entering within it — at this time, this is also named the pāramitā of dhyāna, fulfilled and complete.

This, then, briefly concludes the practice-dharma-gates of dhyāna common to the three vehicles. Within this, the dharma-gates are without limit — how, then, could one who wishes to explain further the essential practices for entering the path ever hope to set them all forth in full?
Shi Chan Boluomi Cidi Famen, Fascicle Ten, ends here.

This closing paragraph functions as a summary index of nearly every advanced attainment named across fascicles 8 through 10 — the summit dhyāna, the buddha-wisdom samādhi, the samādhi free of contention, the four kinds of eloquence, the supernormal powers and transformations — gathered together as the reward of the non-destructive path's full completion. The treatise's very last line is worth sitting with: rather than closing with a triumphant flourish, it closes with a question — "how could one who wishes to explain further the essential practices for entering the path ever hope to set them all forth in full?" — an author's own acknowledgment, in the text's final surviving words, that the subject has outrun the book.

quiz.q: In the lion's four leaps for transcendence, which matching is correct?
options: forward: forward; backward: backward; right: sideways into root dhyāna; left: sideways into contemplative dhyāna
quiz.why: Leaping forward illustrates forward transcendence, backward backward, right sideways into the root dhyānas, and left sideways into contemplative dhyāna.

quiz.q: What does the simile of the yellow and white lions show?
options: śrāvakas like the yellow lion only reach from the first to the third dhyāna; bodhisattvas like the white lion leap to cessation
quiz.why: The śrāvaka's transcendence, like the yellow lion's leap, goes only from the first to the third dhyāna; the bodhisattva's, like the white lion's, reaches all the way to cessation.

quiz.q: In the closing, what do practitioners of the two vehicles and bodhisattvas each attain with these dhyānas?
options: the two vehicles: great-strength arhats; bodhisattvas: the twenty-five samādhis and fulfilled dhyāna-pāramitā
quiz.why: Practitioners of the two vehicles become liberated in both respects, great-strength arhats; bodhisattvas obtain the twenty-five samādhis, break the twenty-five states of existence, and fulfill the dhyāna-pāramitā.
